skill.name: wsdiscovery
skill.description: Use WS-Discovery to discover and enumerate ONVIF cameras, NVRs, and IoT devices on authorized networks.
skill.summary: Discovers WS-Discovery and ONVIF devices, then summarizes device identity, service endpoints, and metadata.
skill.author: BrownFineSecurity

security_audit.summary: Several Ruby backtick alerts are Markdown formatting false positives, and the hardcoded IP alerts are private examples or a protocol multicast address. The skill still carries medium dual-use risk because it directs agents to run wsdiscovery for network reconnaissance and does not require explicit authorization before scanning.

remediation.issue: Network discovery can be run against arbitrary targets.
remediation.suggestion: Add an instruction to confirm the user owns the network or has written authorization before running wsdiscovery.

remediation.issue: Broadcast or multicast discovery can enumerate many devices at once.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation before using multicast discovery, and limit it to approved local network segments.

remediation.issue: External command examples do not mention safe target handling.
remediation.suggestion: Document that targets should be validated as hostnames, IP addresses, or approved multicast addresses before command execution.

semantic_findings.title: Missing Authorization Boundary for Network Discovery
semantic_findings.description: The scan workflow asks for a target hostname or IP and then runs WS-Discovery, but it does not require confirmation that the target is owned or authorized. This can enable scanning outside approved assessment scope.

content.value_statement: Finding ONVIF cameras and IoT devices can be slow when device inventories are incomplete. This skill guides authorized WS-Discovery scans and summarizes device metadata and service endpoints.
actual_capabilities: Guides use of the wsdiscovery command against a hostname, IP address, or approved multicast target.
Supports basic, verbose, JSON, text, and quiet output workflows documented by the skill.
Identifies ONVIF cameras, NVRs, printers, media devices, and other WS-Discovery enabled equipment.
Extracts device IP addresses, ports, endpoint references, device types, manufacturers, models, and versions.
Reports service endpoints, metadata versions, serial numbers, firmware versions, and location information when available.
Helps prepare discovered service endpoints for later authorized ONVIF testing.
limitations: It only finds devices that support and respond to WS-Discovery.
It depends on the wsdiscovery command being available in the iothackbot bin directory.
Results can be limited by routing, firewalls, multicast controls, or device configuration.
It does not authenticate to devices, exploit vulnerabilities, or verify device security posture.

use_cases.title: Inventory ONVIF Cameras
use_cases.description: Map cameras and NVRs on an approved network segment, then record model and firmware details.

use_cases.title: Troubleshoot Device Discovery
use_cases.description: Check whether expected cameras, printers, or media devices respond to WS-Discovery requests.

use_cases.title: Prepare IoT Assessments
use_cases.description: Collect service endpoints and metadata before deeper authorized ONVIF or IoT testing.

prompt_templates.title: Find Devices on One Host
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner discovery against a known authorized host.
prompt_templates.prompt: Discover WS-Discovery devices on 192.168.1.100. Summarize any device identity, service endpoint, and manufacturer details.

prompt_templates.title: Run Verbose Discovery
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review when full protocol responses are useful.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a verbose WS-Discovery scan for the approved target host and explain the device metadata fields in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Inventory Summary
prompt_templates.scenario: Structured reporting for an authorized camera inventory.
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan the approved WS-Discovery target and produce an inventory summary with IP, port, device type, model, firmware, and service endpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Assess a Local Segment
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced multicast discovery on a scoped local network.
prompt_templates.prompt: After confirming authorization, use WS-Discovery multicast on the local segment and prioritize devices that expose ONVIF service endpoints.

output_examples.input: Discover ONVIF devices on an approved camera host.
output_examples.output: The skill runs a basic discovery workflow and returns a concise list of responding devices, including address, device type, manufacturer, model, and service endpoint details when present.
The skill requests full protocol details, then explains endpoint references, scopes, XAddrs, metadata versions, and any device identity fields in readable language.

output_examples.input: Build an inventory from a local multicast discovery.
output_examples.output: The skill confirms the approved scope, runs local discovery, and summarizes all discovered WS-Discovery devices by type, location, service endpoint, and follow-up priority.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization and scope before scanning any host or network segment.
Use the narrowest target that answers the inventory question before using multicast discovery.
Save discovered service endpoints with device identity details for traceable follow-up testing.
anti_patterns: Do not scan third-party networks or public targets without explicit authorization.
Do not treat missing WS-Discovery responses as proof that no cameras or IoT devices exist.
Do not publish serial numbers, firmware versions, or service endpoints from sensitive environments.

faq.question: What protocol does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses WS-Discovery, a discovery protocol commonly used by ONVIF cameras, NVRs, printers, and media devices.

faq.question: Can it find every camera on a network?
faq.answer: No. It only finds devices that support WS-Discovery and can receive the discovery request.

faq.question: Does it perform vulnerability scanning?
faq.answer: No. It discovers devices and metadata, but it does not authenticate, exploit, or verify vulnerabilities.

faq.question: What information can it report?
faq.answer: It can report addresses, ports, device UUIDs, types, manufacturer data, models, versions, locations, and service endpoints.

faq.question: Is multicast discovery supported?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents multicast discovery, but it should only be used on approved local network segments.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
